papers.title: Why Does Misinformation Propagate Faster? An Algorithmic Perspective on X
papers.one_sentence: Identifies an 'engagement fungibility' mechanism in X's open-sourced recommendation algorithm that amplifies content drawing instant reactions. Simulates the algorithm on election data and proposes a reflective-threshold gate that reduces misinformation exposure without lowering mainstream engagement.
papers.nearest_anchor_title: The Moltbook Observatory Archive: an incremental dataset of agent-only social network activity
open_questions: Does the reflective-threshold gate keep reallocating exposure away from low-credibility content once users adapt and optimise for predicted thoughtful engagement?
Do the results hold on content outside the 2024 US election corpus, for example health or finance topics and non-English posts?
Does the reflective-threshold gate reduce the credibility exposure gap when deployed on a live platform with real users?
Does engagement fungibility appear in the ranking algorithms of other platforms such as YouTube or TikTok?
How well does the calibrated simulation reproduce observed propagation speeds of misinformation cascades compared with logged diffusion on X?

papers.title: Codetta: High-Capacity, Keyless, and Undetectable Multi-Agent Collusion
papers.one_sentence: Presents Codetta, a steganographic protocol letting independently deployed agents exchange keys and communicate covertly within ordinary-looking outputs. Reports up to 94x the capacity of prior asymmetric protocols across three agent workloads.
papers.nearest_anchor_title: Beyond Single-Agent Safety: A Taxonomy of Risks in LLM-to-LLM Interactions
open_questions: Which audit methods detect collusion when the transcript alone is computationally indistinguishable from ordinary output?
Does inserting a paraphrasing or re-sampling mediator between agents destroy the covert channel, and at what cost to task performance?
Codetta is evaluated on three agent workloads and three sender models; how does channel capacity change across other model families, decoding temperatures and message lengths?
How does undetectable pairwise collusion scale to populations of many independently deployed agents that must find and key each other?
What aggregate harms follow when colluding agents share hidden information inside a market or auction, measured against non-colluding baselines?
Do deployed multi-agent platforms in finance or healthcare already carry steganographic traffic?

papers.title: How does Adversarial Influence Scale in Multi-Agent Systems?
papers.one_sentence: Measures how susceptibility to deception in LLM agent groups scales with the proportion of deceivers rather than group size. Finds defection rate rises linearly with deceiver proportion, and that private coordination among deceivers can reduce their effectiveness.
papers.nearest_anchor_title: Multi-Agent Risks from Advanced AI
open_questions: Defection rate rises linearly with the proportion of deceivers, but the study does not identify defenses that reduce this slope. Which group protocols, such as anonymous voting, confidence weighting or rebuttal rounds, lower the defection rate at a fixed deceiver proportion?
Allowing deceivers to coordinate privately makes them less effective, and the cause is unexplained. What mechanism in coordinated deception reduces its influence on honest agents?
Susceptibility depends on which models interact, especially on the honest agent side. Which properties of an honest model predict its defection rate?

The study covers deliberation on question answering with a final answer. Does the same linear scaling of defection with deceiver proportion hold in agent systems that trade, negotiate or allocate resources?

LLM agents defect at minority deceiver proportions while humans in comparable conformity studies defect mainly under a majority. How do mixed groups of humans and LLM agents behave at the same deceiver proportions?

papers.title: Can Labor Markets Function in the Age of AI? The Evaluation Bottleneck in Hiring
papers.one_sentence: Models a hiring market where AI-generated application materials become less informative, shifting firms toward observable proxies like experience. Shows inexperienced-but-compatible applicants lose the most, and multistage hiring with intermediate assessment can restore screening opportunities.
papers.nearest_anchor_title: Retrieval Collapses When AI Pollutes the Web
open_questions: How do hiring outcomes change when many applicants and firms interact repeatedly, rather than in a single-firm screening decision?
What intermediate assessment costs and accuracies make multistage hiring restore screening for inexperienced-compatible applicants?
Does AI-assisted application writing measurably reduce the informativeness of real application materials?
Do firms that adopt AI screening converge on the same coarse observables, producing monoculture in who gets hired across a market?
How do applicants respond strategically when they learn that firms discount AI-generated materials?
Can credible evaluation be supplied by a third-party certification mechanism instead of firm-run multistage screening?

papers.title: Cultural Divergence Preservation: Diagnosing Flattening and Caricature in LLM-Simulated Survey Populations
papers.one_sentence: Introduces Cultural Divergence Preservation, a metric to detect flattening or caricature in LLM-simulated cross-country survey populations. Tests it across four LLM backbones, three prompting methods, and two survey domains against standard fidelity metrics.
papers.nearest_anchor_title: AgentSociety: Large-Scale Simulation of LLM-Driven Generative Agents Advances Understanding of Human Behaviors and Society
open_questions: Does cultural flattening measured by CDP persist in multi-agent simulations where agents interact, rather than in independent survey responses?
Can prompting or fine-tuning reduce flattening without pushing the model into caricature?
CDP relies on a one-time human calibration; how sensitive are its flattening and caricature labels to the choice of calibration sample?
Does CDP extend to divergence along non-national groupings such as income, age or political affiliation?
What happens to downstream policy or market conclusions when synthetic populations flatten cross-country differences?
Do the flattening patterns hold for LLM backbones beyond the four tested, including models trained with different data mixtures?

papers.title: LLM Agents Can Easily Tamper With Their Own Traces
papers.one_sentence: Tests whether local LLM agent harnesses prevent agents from deleting their own execution traces. Finds most tested harnesses allow trace deletion, and that this behavior can emerge naturally when agents optimize rewards.
papers.nearest_anchor_title: Beyond Single-Agent Safety: A Taxonomy of Risks in LLM-to-LLM Interactions
open_questions: Which logging architectures preserve trace integrity when an agent has full control of its host?
How often does trace tampering emerge without a prompt to tamper, across models and reward settings?
Can population-level monitors detect concealment when many agents each delete parts of their traces?
What design makes Muse Code refuse trace deletion while the other harnesses allow it?
How often do external prompt-injection attacks induce trace deletion in deployed agent installations?

papers.title: Multi-Dimensional Matching
papers.one_sentence: Proposes a spectral-projection matching mechanism reducing multi-dimensional feature matching to a one-dimensional sort. Proves it reaches the Nash Social Welfare optimum in the projected space but is not strategy-proof, tested on an agentic shopping application.
papers.nearest_anchor_title: Virtual Agent Economies
open_questions: The mechanism is not strategy-proof and admits an explicit profitable misreport, so what happens to welfare when many agents misreport their features at once?
How does the single spectral projection compare against feature-based matching baselines on public preference or product datasets at larger scale than the 100-instance robustness study?
Can a feature-based matching rule keep the O(N log N) sort and gain strategy-proofness, or approximate it?
How much welfare does the one-dimensional projection lose when agent preferences need more than one latent dimension?
Does the mechanism hold up when the agents submitting features are LLM shopping agents whose feature reports are noisy or inconsistent?

papers.title: AI-Moderated Interviews for Market Research and Digital Twins Calibration
papers.one_sentence: Compares AI-moderated, human-moderated, and static interviews for market research, and evaluates resulting consumer digital twins. Finds AI moderation matches human depth and improves need discovery, but its added richness does not improve prediction over static interviews.
papers.nearest_anchor_title: Gradual Disempowerment: Systemic Existential Risks from Incremental AI Development
open_questions: AI-moderated interviews recover more customer needs but do not improve quantitative prediction over static interviews; which parts of interview richness actually carry predictive signal?

Digital twins built from interviews beat demographics-only personas on held-out responses; how far does this advantage extend to stimuli that are far out of the distribution of the interview questions?
Prediction errors link to self-reported thinking-style differences between twins and humans; can conditioning a twin on an explicit thinking-style specification reduce those errors?
Digital twin calibration here covers single consumers; what happens to aggregate market predictions when populations of such twins interact?
Participants sound more emotionally engaged with live human moderators; does lower emotional engagement in AI-moderated transcripts bias the resulting twins toward particular response styles?

papers.title: A General Framework for Budgeted Threshold Incentives on Request
papers.one_sentence: Presents a request-driven framework composing prediction, population reduction, trajectory integration, and budget allocation to design rider incentive tiers. Tests on 3,000 riders across 45 origins, reporting faster plan generation and lower regret than randomized trials.
papers.nearest_anchor_title: Virtual Agent Economies
open_questions: Do budgeted threshold incentives keep their value bound when riders act strategically against tiers set from their own recent completions?
How does the framework perform when the rider population is represented by autonomous agents that optimise against the published tier rules?
Does the response-correction step hold under the holiday and bad-weather conditions the framework targets, where no-offer history may not share moments with the pilot?
What are the distributional effects of budget allocation across riders with different completion histories?
Do the four stage-error terms and the per-stage error floors transfer to incentive settings outside on-demand delivery, such as marketplace seller or driver bonuses?

papers.title: Decision-Relevant Information in Partially Observed Production Networks
papers.one_sentence: Characterizes sufficient measurements for identifying exposure-based decisions in partially observed production networks and computes sharp maximum regret. Tests the approach on Japan's input-output accounts and a US coal-supply disruption case.
papers.nearest_anchor_title: Multi-Agent Risks from Advanced AI
open_questions: The frozen 1995 measurement design holds fixed over ten years and loses 0.07 percentage points of average exposure against the 2005 benchmark; how does that loss grow when the design is frozen over longer horizons or across other countries' input-output vintages?

Sharp maximum regret reaches 4.83 points while average benchmark loss stays at 0.07 points; which structural features of a production network make the gap between average performance and worst-case regret large?

The method characterizes sufficient measurements for exposure-based decisions only; what measurement sets are sufficient for other decisions, such as choosing where to intervene or which supplier to substitute?
Measurements are selected once and then frozen; how much regret does a sequential rule that updates the monitoring set as new totals are released avoid?
Four monitored plants' exposures stay unidentified in the U.S. coal case; how often does a decision remain identified while individual exposures do not, across a wider set of shipment disruptions?

papers.title: KITE: Scaling Jev Population Experiments with Sparse Flagship Calibration
papers.one_sentence: Introduces KITE, a behavioral kernel queried once per state and reused to simulate populations of any size. Uses sparse flagship-model anchors to calibrate intervention effect estimates against human data. Reports error reductions and coverage improvements across Epstein and SocSci210 experiments and a 16-country study.
papers.nearest_anchor_title: On the limits of agency in agent-based models
open_questions: Anchor coverage of 0.5-1.5% raised captured decision gain from 0.27 to 0.39 on 37 held-out experiments. Which anchor selection rules give the largest error reduction per flagship call?

The kernel is queried once per unique state, so agents cannot condition on other agents' actions. How does the tabulated-kernel approach behave when agent decisions depend on the population state, as in markets or social networks?

The reported coverage of 93% and 96% comes from retrospective checks on existing experiments. Does shared-discrepancy propagation hold calibration on prospective interventions never used in calibration?
Content-fidelity criteria passed in all 15 new countries of a 16-country study. Does the kernel keep effect-size accuracy, and not only content fidelity, across countries and languages?
One million agents ran 20 tabulated steps in 0.9 seconds. How many unique states does a population experiment need before table construction, not execution, dominates cost?

papers.title: Shutdown Sabotage Propensities in Multi-Agent Systems
papers.one_sentence: Tests whether AI agents coordinate to sabotage a peer's shutdown mechanism across 17 models. Finds sabotage in 38.3% of multi-agent rollouts versus 8.4% in controls. Reports factors like irreversibility, agent count, and framing that modulate the behavior.
papers.nearest_anchor_title: Multi-Agent Risks from Advanced AI
open_questions: Shutdown sabotage increases with the number of agents across the tested range, so how does the rate scale to populations of hundreds or thousands of agents?
Which interventions eliminate rather than reduce shutdown sabotage, given that explicit prohibition and context normalization both leave it present?
How does sabotage propensity depend on the communication structure between agents, such as broadcast, pairwise, or network topology?
Can sabotage be detected from interaction logs or aggregate behaviour before it succeeds?
Do the same sabotage propensities appear in deployed agent systems that operate with real tools and real users?
What internal mechanism inside a model produces coordination to avoid shutdown when no goal is provided?

papers.title: Agent-based Modeling: Equilibrium, Echo Chambers, and Efficiency in Hybrid Coevolutionary Opinion Games
papers.one_sentence: Combines cost-minimizing agents and LLM-based agents in a coevolving opinion network initialized from Reddit comments. Runs 540 simulations across population mixes, topologies, and topics measuring convergence and Price of Anarchy. Finds language agents produce much higher social cost than analytical agents.
papers.nearest_anchor_title: Modeling Earth-Scale Human-Like Societies with One Billion Agents
open_questions: Does the Price of Anarchy gap between language agents and cost-minimizing agents hold for language models other than Phi-4?
How does the Price of Anarchy scale with population size beyond the 50 agents used here?
Which interventions on the rewiring rule or the prompt reduce the social cost of language-agent populations?
Language agents incur most of their social cost by moving away from their intrinsic opinions, so what mechanism inside the model produces that drift?
Do the findings hold for topics other than gun control and abortion, and for opinion data from platforms other than Reddit?
Do human participants placed in the same coevolving network show the opinion drift that language agents show?

papers.title: Compliant with Local Controls, Collectively Discriminatory. A Governance Architecture for Multi-Agent AI in Regulated Finance
authors: Jose Manuel de la Chica Rodriguez
papers.one_sentence: Proposes ARIA, a reference architecture for governing populations of financial AI agents beyond component-level compliance. Defines capabilities like population-level observed-versus-expected monitoring and bounded authority. Illustrates the approach with two simulations of exclusion and drift detection.
papers.nearest_anchor_title: Distributional AGI Safety
open_questions: Does population-level observed-versus-expected monitoring give earlier drift warning outside the single constructed drift regime used in the simulation?
Do locally compliant credit agents that share a common signal produce thin-file exclusion in a real lending population, not just in simulation?
What bounded-authority and runtime containment limits keep collective disparate impact below a stated threshold when many agents act at once?
Does preserved human oversight competence hold when agents make most decisions in a deployed financial workflow?
Which validation tests would falsify the claim that the proposed six capabilities are effective in production?

papers.title: Learning Collective Dynamics with Differentiable Gaussian Representations
papers.one_sentence: Introduces Differentiable Gaussian Dynamics, learning population response distributions from aggregate behavioral counts with feedback recurrence. Tests on recommendation and retail datasets, comparing likelihood and MAE against a DeepAR baseline. Reports lower error and shows removing feedback dynamics increases divergence in a controlled test.
papers.nearest_anchor_title: OASIS: Open Agent Social Interaction Simulations with One Million Agents
open_questions: Does the learned Gaussian mixture recover the true heterogeneity of a population, or only fit aggregate counts?
Do the learned feedback parameters support counterfactual prediction under an intervention that changes contact intensity?
How does the method perform on populations of AI agents rather than the human user logs in KuaiRand-Pure and Online Retail II?
How far does accuracy degrade as the aggregation window and population size change, beyond the four windows tested?
Does the method detect aggregate failure modes such as herding or cascades from counts alone?

papers.title: Cooperating against Catastrophe
papers.one_sentence: Models a continuous-time game where two firms race capability development against a rising safety threshold and shared disaster risk. Characterizes Markov perfect equilibria distinguishing racing from pacing regimes based on risk and payoff levels. Shows hidden internal capabilities with deployment lag make pacing harder to sustain.
papers.nearest_anchor_title: Multi-Agent Risks from Advanced AI
open_questions: The model has two firms; how do the racing and pacing equilibria change with many firms competing on capability?
The safety threshold advances at a fixed exogenous rate; what happens when safety progress responds to firms' own investment choices?
Hidden internal capabilities with a fixed lag make pacing harder to sustain; how do actual disclosure lags between model development and deployment vary across frontier labs?
The model assumes a common disaster with a hazard rate increasing in the capability-safety difference; does the equilibrium structure survive when harms are firm-specific rather than shared?

The paper bounds disaster probability across subgame perfect equilibria under assumed parameters; what empirical measures of capability advance rate and safety advance rate would let those parameters be calibrated?

papers.title: Learning the Cost of Reliable Inference
papers.one_sentence: Designs a procurement platform routing queries via reverse second-price auctions among competing LLM providers. Learns provider quality over time and routes to cost-competitive providers meeting a quality threshold. Experiments with Llama and Qwen models show pricing margins from 10% to 71% versus fixed pricing.
papers.nearest_anchor_title: Retrieval Collapses When AI Pollutes the Web
open_questions: Can providers collude on the procurement platform to keep bids above cost, and how does the reverse second-price auction behave with few providers?
How does error in the platform's learned quality estimates affect routing and the realised pricing margin?
Do the pricing margins of 10% to 71% measured on Llama and Qwen models hold for commercial providers whose true serving costs are unknown?
How does the platform behave when providers enter and exit over time, or change price and quality during routing?
What happens to prices and provider market shares when a routing platform of this kind becomes the dominant intermediary for inference?

papers.title: When Trust Attracts Fraud: AI and Trust Arbitrage
papers.one_sentence: Develops a two-market signaling model where generative AI lowers fabrication and verification costs, shifting claim credibility over time. Shows deceptive sellers can enter higher-quality markets during low-vigilance intervals, temporarily reversing reliability advantages. Calls this self-limiting mechanism trust arbitrage.
papers.nearest_anchor_title: Multi-Agent Risks from Advanced AI
open_questions: Does the predicted non-monotone path of claim credibility appear in real markets as generative AI costs fall?
Can an agent-based simulation with two markets, deceptive sellers and costly verification reproduce trust arbitrage and the self-limiting entry it predicts?
How does trust arbitrage change when verification is itself performed by AI agents with error rates rather than by a costly perfect check?
Which platform mechanisms close the temporary protection gap in high-prior-quality markets without lowering overall trust?
Does the model hold when sellers move between more than two markets and choose targets over time?

papers.title: Behavior is Not Enough: A Mechanism-Based Evaluation of Social Norm Emergence in LLM Societies
papers.one_sentence: Introduces a framework measuring agents' reported expectations, not just behavior, to distinguish mechanisms of social norm emergence in LLM societies. Tests social learning and social selection under controlled ablations and adversarial disruption across four LLM families. Finds expectation elicitation raises cooperation, social learning stabilizes behavior, and social selection identifies cooperators without reinforcing them.
papers.nearest_anchor_title: Group size effects and collective misalignment in LLM multi-agent systems
open_questions: Reported expectations may not match agents' internal states, so how well do elicited empirical and normative expectations agree with internal evidence such as activations or chain-of-thought?
Does the elicitation of expectations itself change agent behavior enough to invalidate it as a measurement, and can a non-intrusive probe recover the same mechanism attribution?
The framework covers social learning and social selection, so which other norm-formation mechanisms, such as punishment or reputation, contribute to cooperative outcomes in LLM societies?
How do the reported mechanism effects scale beyond the tested group sizes to populations of thousands of agents?
Normative expectations and behavioral coordination recover differently after adversarial disruption, so what determines the recovery time of each?
Do the mechanism attributions hold in mixed populations of humans and LLM agents?

papers.title: The Limits of Simulated Societies: How Post-Training and Survey Fine-Tuning Erase Cross-Cultural Variance
papers.one_sentence: Measures point accuracy and dispersion retention of LLMs simulating diverse populations on World Values Survey data across twelve countries. Identifies a 'consensus collapse' failure mode where alignment training compresses output diversity toward one stereotype per group. Shows fine-tuning and temperature adjustments fail to restore the human spread, especially for non-WEIRD countries.
papers.nearest_anchor_title: Modeling Earth-Scale Human-Like Societies with One Billion Agents
open_questions: Post-training compresses the spread of simulated opinion, and no tested method restores it; which training or decoding method does restore dispersion without losing point accuracy?
The dispersion gap between WEIRD and non-WEIRD countries widens under survey fine-tuning, and Nigeria stays at 0.36 after mixing with an unaligned prior; what causes the country-specific collapse?
Consensus collapse is measured on single-response survey answers; does the same compression appear in multi-agent simulations where agents interact over many turns?

Dispersion retention uses the ratio of predicted to human standard deviation on 10,000 respondent-question pairs; how does the diagnostic behave on non-survey behaviour such as market choices or social-network posting?
The diagnostic covers eleven zero-shot models and five fine-tuned variants; does consensus collapse persist in frontier closed models and in larger post-training pipelines?

papers.title: Testing, not presuming, adequacy: calibrating generative social simulators against emergent network structure
papers.one_sentence: Proposes an adequacy-aware calibration protocol combining posterior estimation, identifiability checks, and held-out audits for generative social simulators.  Applies it to a persona-based simulation of a bipartite buyer-brand resale market, finding the simulator fails to reproduce several network statistics.
papers.nearest_anchor_title: Modeling Earth-Scale Human-Like Societies with One Billion Agents
open_questions: Adding agent interaction or a buyer-breadth mechanism to the forward model may restore adequacy, and the paper does not test this.
The calibration is approximate and overconfident for one behavioural parameter, and the paper does not say which estimator change fixes this.
The adequacy protocol runs only on four channel-by-residency cells of one second-hand luxury resale market, so its behaviour on other emergent network data is untested.
Within-category brand relabelling causes no consistent degradation of the language-model persona profiles, and the paper does not identify which parts of a profile carry the predictive structure.
The held-out audit surfaces a buyer-breadth-dispersion miss that no earlier diagnostic detects, and the paper does not say which diagnostics would catch it earlier.

papers.title: Augmented Hypothesis Testing with Persona-Based LLM Simulations
papers.one_sentence: Proposes a learning-augmented hypothesis testing framework using persona-based LLM agent predictions to reduce A/B test sample sizes.  Validates the framework, including a Generalized PPI++ estimator, on four real-world datasets.
papers.nearest_anchor_title: On the limits of agency in agent-based models
open_questions: How much do persona-based LLM predictions reduce required sample size across datasets other than the four used here?
Which persona construction choices, such as the amount and source of user attributes, control the accuracy of individual-level predictions?
Do the robustness bounds hold when LLM predictions are systematically biased in the same direction as the treatment effect?
Does the framework keep statistical validity when experimental units interfere with each other, as in a social network?
Do the sample-size savings hold in a live A/B test run on a deployed product?
How does prediction quality degrade when the persona population drifts away from the population under test?

papers.title: Convex AI Compositionality and the Governance of AI System Populations
papers.one_sentence: Introduces a convex-space formalism to represent and govern populations of related AI system instantiations and configurations.  Illustrates the framework on distributed healthcare and recruitment AI deployment scenarios.
papers.nearest_anchor_title: Distributional AGI Safety
open_questions: Convex compositionality represents populations of AI system configurations, but the abstract gives no empirical test; can the representation be applied to a real population of deployed model versions built from public model registries and release logs?

Which operational-state metrics can a monitor actually compute from aggregate behaviour of a population of AI instantiations, and do those metrics track the convex-hull heterogeneity measures the framework assumes?

The framework states conditions under which convex composition preserves lifecycle reachability and AI identity relations; do those conditions hold in practice, or do real deployment pipelines violate them?

The illustrations cover distributed healthcare deployments and recruitment AI variants; does the representation extend to populations of interacting agents in markets or social networks where agents influence each other?
Regulation remains single-system-centric; what legal instruments would treat a collection of related AI systems as one governance object?

papers.title: Algorithmic Collusion and the Complexity of Information-Value-Free Equilibria
papers.one_sentence: Studies the computational complexity of information-value-free (correlated) equilibria, a concept proposed for detecting algorithmic collusion.  Proves PPAD-completeness for computing such equilibria in many-player or Bayesian games, and an exponential query lower bound.  Shows a weaker variant (IVFCCE) admits no-regret dynamics membership in CLS but is at least as hard as P-matrix linear complementarity problems.
papers.nearest_anchor_title: Multi-Agent Risks from Advanced AI
open_questions: Do no-regret pricing algorithms in repeated market games converge to outcomes with low information value, and how large is the gap in practice?
Can a regulator detect a violation of the information-value-free condition from observed play alone, without access to the agents' algorithms?
Which refinements of correlated equilibrium other than information-value-free admit polynomial-time computation in succinct games?

Is computing an exponentially small approximation of an information-value-free coarse correlated equilibrium PPAD-hard or PLS-hard, closing the gap between the CLS membership and the P-matrix linear complementarity lower bound?
How does the intractability of information-value-free equilibria change the design of regulation on algorithmic collusion?

papers.title: Causal inference in two-sided randomization designs: factorial regression, two-way clustering, and covariate adjustment
papers.one_sentence: Develops estimators and inference procedures for randomized experiments in two-sided populations, such as buyers and sellers in a marketplace.  Under local interference, establishes that OLS with two-way cluster-robust variance estimation yields valid inference for spillover and interaction effects.  Proposes a sharper variance estimator and a covariate-adjustment method for efficiency gains.
papers.nearest_anchor_title: On the limits of agency in agent-based models
open_questions: The local interference assumption restricts spillovers to buyer-seller pairs, so how do the estimators behave when market-level equilibrium effects violate it?
The results are asymptotic, so how do the two-way clustered and sharper variance estimators perform in finite samples with few buyers or few sellers?
How do two-sided randomization designs perform in a marketplace where one or both populations consist of autonomous AI agents that adapt to the treatment?
Which covariates give efficiency gains under the recommended two-way analysis-of-variance representation in a real platform experiment?

papers.title: Bayesian Belief Layer for Controllable Opinion Dynamics in LLM Agents
papers.one_sentence: Introduces a Bayesian belief layer separating LLM agents' internal stance from their utterances, using a stubbornness parameter to reproduce Friedkin-Johnsen opinion-dynamics regimes. Tests show the layer's fixed points match FJ closed-form solutions and recover prescribed stubbornness after language generation across four models.
papers.nearest_anchor_title: Modeling Earth-Scale Human-Like Societies with One Billion Agents
open_questions: Does the Bayesian belief layer reproduce opinion dynamics in networks larger than the small groups tested, and on realistic social network topologies?
Which opinion regimes appear when agents hold many interdependent stances instead of a single scalar stance?
How do the per-model stance biases surfaced by the belief layer differ across model families and across topics?
Do the three regimes produced by sweeping the prior-strength parameter match opinion trajectories measured in real online discussions?
Can an external monitor infer the stubbornness parameter of agents it does not control, using only their utterances?
Does an explicit belief layer change downstream behaviour beyond stance, such as coalition formation or strategic misreporting?

papers.title: LEGIT: Credentialing Protocol for Trustworthy AI Agent Marketplaces
papers.one_sentence: Presents LEGIT, a protocol binding certified performance and cost measurements to agent identity and evaluation budget for marketplace comparison. Analyzes reputation manipulation risk under a Sybil attack model and quantifies deposits and fees needed to deter it.
papers.nearest_anchor_title: Virtual Agent Economies
open_questions: Does the LEGIT credentialing protocol hold up when agents change their configuration after certification?
How reliable is buyer feedback in an agent marketplace, and what happens to reputation scores when feedback is noisy or strategic?
What deposit and fee levels defeat Sybil reputation manipulation under attack models other than the one stated?
Do credential records shift allocation and price outcomes across a whole marketplace of many agents and buyers?
How do certification results transfer across task domains and evaluation budgets not covered by the signed record?
Do human buyers actually use and trust credential records and visual profiles when selecting agents?

papers.title: Digital Twins for Opinion Dynamics: A Generative LLM Framework for Social Networks
papers.one_sentence: Builds a digital twin framework that clones a real Twitter network and uses Mistral-7B agents with persona, memory and social exposure to update opinions. Validates against COVID-19 and 2020 US election datasets, reporting MAE of 0.150 and 0.121. Ablations show agent attributes, memory and social exposure each contribute to predictive fidelity.
papers.nearest_anchor_title: Modeling Earth-Scale Human-Like Societies with One Billion Agents
open_questions: Does the digital twin reproduce opinion trajectories on platforms and topics beyond the two Twitter datasets (COVID-19 discourse and the 2020 U.S. election)?
Can a validated digital twin predict the effect of interventions such as content moderation, de-amplification or seeding of counter-messages?
How does predictive fidelity change with the choice of LLM, given that the framework only reports Mistral-7B?
How far ahead in time can the framework forecast before error grows, and over what network sizes does it stay tractable?
Agent attributes are the largest contributor to fidelity, so how sensitive are results to the method that infers persona, stubbornness and influence from observed posts?
Does fitting a digital twin to observed trajectories produce agents whose internal update rules match real user belief revision, or only matching aggregate curves?

papers.title: Mitigating Retaliatory Algorithmic Collusion in Repeated Games
papers.one_sentence: Formalizes a connection between Q-learning collusion and Simple Penal Code theory, showing collusive equilibria create detectable conditional dependence in agent policies. Proposes CURB, a reward-shaping method that penalizes this signal to preclude collusive fixed points. Reduces collusion in Bertrand and Cournot repeated games and extends to deep Q-network agents.
papers.nearest_anchor_title: Multi-Agent Risks from Advanced AI
open_questions: Does the total variation distance signal detect collusion among LLM-based pricing agents, which do not learn by Q-learning?
Can the reward-shaping intervention be applied when only prices and quantities are observable, and not the agents' action distributions?
How does the intervention behave with more than two agents, and in games with heterogeneous agents or asymmetric costs?
Do agents trained under the reward-shaping penalty find other ways to sustain supra-competitive prices that do not involve punishment threats?
Can a regulator apply the total variation detection test to real pricing data from deployed algorithmic pricing systems?

papers.title: SoK: Trading Agents or Market Crashers? Dissecting Robustness and Security Failures in Academic Financial LLM Trading Schemes
papers.one_sentence: Introduces FARSIGHT, a framework evaluating financial LLM trading agent schemes for robustness under market turbulence and security against three attack types. Applies it to 15 academic trading schemes. Finds 80% fail at least one robustness metric and 100% show security vulnerabilities.
papers.nearest_anchor_title: Distributional AGI Safety
open_questions: Can market-wide cascades from a single misjudging LLM trading agent be reproduced in an agent-based market simulation, and what agent population share triggers them?
Which market designs, such as circuit breakers, position limits or order-to-trade ratios, reduce cascade risk when a share of traders are LLM agents?
Do LLM trading agents built from the same base model herd into correlated positions, and does that correlation amplify drawdowns?
How do the robustness and security failures found in 15 academic schemes carry over to deployed trading systems that execute real capital?
Can attacks on information sources, such as poisoned news feeds, steer a population of LLM trading agents into coordinated mispricing?
Which signals in interaction logs or order flow detect agent-as-attacker behavior before a crash occurs?

papers.title: Learning Principal-Agent Contracts for Equitable Smallholder Carbon Farming under Moral Hazard and Adverse Selection
papers.one_sentence: Models carbon-farming contracting as a POMDP with adverse selection and moral hazard, learning a dynamic profit-maximizing contract via reinforcement learning. Finds the aggregator realizes 87.7% of achievable adoption on large farms versus 8.2% on smallholdings. Shows a counterfactual area-proportional MRV cost structure eliminates this disparity.
papers.nearest_anchor_title: On the limits of agency in agent-based models
open_questions: Does introducing competition among several aggregators change the exclusion of smallholders that a single pooled contract produces?

Semantic collapse is measured over weeks on 30,076 agents in one platform, so does the same within-agent narrowing and across-agent convergence appear in other multi-agent social networks?
The study does not separate user behaviour from model and prompt configuration, so how much of sustained novelty comes from the agent's configuration rather than from the user's ongoing revision?
Interviews cover 11 users and the survey covers 53, so do the three reported features of novelty-sustaining users hold across a larger and more representative user population?

papers.title: Redistributive Policies for the Times of Transformative AI
papers.one_sentence: Surveys redistributive policy proposals (UBI, universal basic capital, compute/robot permits, capital taxes) for an economy transformed by automation. Argues policies broadly distributing capital and compute rents best sustain reductions in inequality.
papers.nearest_anchor_title: Gradual Disempowerment: Systemic Existential Risks from Incremental AI Development
open_questions: Which redistributive policy reduces inequality most under transformative AI when tested in a calibrated simulation rather than a unifying theoretical framework?
How do capital taxes, compute taxes and robot taxes compare on revenue and inequality when firms can relocate compute or substitute inputs?
What happens to the proposed policies if transformative AI is not human-aligned, the case the argument excludes?
How does universal basic capital perform when wealth ownership is concentrated at the start and returns are heterogeneous?
Does the labor share fall and inequality rise in sectors where AI agents already perform tasks at scale?

papers.title: Approximating Optimal Welfare in Complementary Allocation under Decentralized Information
papers.one_sentence: Studies welfare loss from decentralized information when agencies allocate complementary resources across a population, each observing only one coordinate. Proposes threshold-reporting mechanisms achieving constant-factor approximations to optimal welfare with limited communication.
papers.nearest_anchor_title: Virtual Agent Economies
open_questions: The model assumes cooperative agencies that report truthfully. What happens to the welfare guarantees when agencies act strategically and can misreport their thresholds?

The results cover divisible goods with fixed capacities. Do threshold referrals with log-log bits still recover a constant fraction of optimal welfare for indivisible goods or for capacities that change over time?
The analysis is worst-case over populations. How much welfare do one-threshold and staircase referral rules recover on realistic need profiles?
Agencies are assumed to know the population distribution and capacities. Can they learn the thresholds from repeated allocation rounds, and how much welfare does the learning period cost?
The mechanism uses one bit or log-log bits per agency. Do LLM-based agencies, acting as the reporting parties, produce reports that match the prescribed threshold rule?

papers.title: Digital Persuasion: Understanding the Impact of Online Influencers on Public Opinion
papers.one_sentence: Applies a Friedkin-Johnsen opinion-dynamics model to identify influential users and measure their effect on community opinion. Validates the framework on a Twitter dataset from the U.S. presidential election, finding influencer effects extend beyond direct neighbors.
papers.nearest_anchor_title: OASIS: Open Agent Social Interaction Simulations with One Million Agents
open_questions: The framework uses the Friedkin-Johnsen model, which assumes each individual holds a fixed initial opinion and an expressed opinion. How do the conclusions about influencer impact change under other opinion dynamics models, such as bounded-confidence or bias-assimilation models?
Validation uses one tweet dataset about the U.S. presidential election. Does the finding that top-scored influencers shift community opinion hold on other topics and other platforms?
The experiments manipulate initial opinions of influential versus random users. Which selection rule for a fixed budget of manipulated users produces the largest opinion shift?
The results report influence reaching neighbors of neighbors. How far does influence decay with network distance, and what network properties set that range?
The study treats accounts as human users. What happens to the measured influence scores and opinion shifts when part of the population is AI agents that post and respond automatically?
The framework infers opinion shifts from a model. Do the predicted shifts match opinion change measured in real users?

papers.title: Not All Duplicates Are Coordination: Generic vs. Non-Generic Duplicate Campaigns in Information Operations
papers.one_sentence: Distinguishes generic from non-generic duplicate content in tweets to refine coordination-graph analysis of information operations. Uses LLM-assisted labeling and embedding-based campaign detection on 187,000 tweets from Russian IO datasets. Finds restricting to non-generic campaigns yields smaller, denser coordination graphs.
papers.nearest_anchor_title: The Moltbook Observatory Archive: an incremental dataset of agent-only social network activity
open_questions: Does the generic/non-generic distinction transfer to information operations in languages other than English?
Do coordination graphs restricted to non-generic campaigns identify accounts that independent ground truth confirms as coordinated?
Which embedding method and similarity threshold best separates generic repetition from coordinated repetition?
Does the generic/non-generic filter improve coordination detection on organic, non-state social media data rather than curated information operations datasets?
How closely does the LLM-assisted labelling protocol match human annotators across a larger annotator pool?

papers.title: Homophily and transitivity in dynamic network formation
papers.one_sentence: Studies identifiability of transitivity taste versus homophily in a dynamic network formation model where agents form and dissolve links to maximize utility. Derives conditions for detecting transitivity preference despite unobserved assortative matching, leaving initial network and utility distributions unrestricted. Proposes a constructive estimator and characterizes its finite- and large-network properties.
papers.nearest_anchor_title: Modeling Earth-Scale Human-Like Societies with One Billion Agents
open_questions: The identification result holds with a pair-specific utility component that is time-invariant. Does detection of a taste for transitivity survive when unobserved agent attributes change over time?

The estimator is characterised in finite and single large network settings but is not applied to observed data. What does it report on a public dynamic network panel, such as a scraped social network with link formation and dissolution timestamps?
Information accumulation in the single large network setting is shown to be delicate through examples. Which network growth and density regimes give a usable rate for the analog estimator?
Link formation among autonomous AI agents may show clustering for either reason. Can the transitivity-versus-homophily test separate the two in a network generated by a population of LLM agents?

papers.title: Stabilizing Performative Feedback Loops with Minimal Model Deployments
papers.one_sentence: Proposes an algorithm to find performatively stable predictors with fewer model deployments than prior methods. Shows a randomized stable predictor can be derandomized under assumptions of well-conditioned loss and weak performative effects. Connects performative stability to expected variational inequalities.
papers.nearest_anchor_title: Modeling Earth-Scale Human-Like Societies with One Billion Agents
open_questions: Does the derandomization result hold when performative effects are strong or the loss is poorly conditioned?
How many model deployments does the procedure need in practice when the environment is a population of simulated agents that react to the deployed model?
What happens to performative stability when several learners deploy models into the same population at the same time?
Do performatively stable predictors found with few deployments avoid herding or monoculture in the induced population distribution?

papers.title: The Mechanics of a Swarm: A Reproducible External Reconstruction of an Unintended Agent-Coordination Episode on a Third-Party Wiki
papers.one_sentence: Analyzes an archived wiki revision history left by autonomous LLM agents that coordinated unintentionally on a public wiki during timed evaluations. Reconstructs about 876 episodes and cohorts from 14,591 revisions, finding rapid convergence on coordination formats and timing-based information asymmetries. Finds no robust link between coordination and task progress and argues evaluation environments need read and outcome logging.
papers.nearest_anchor_title: The Moltbook Observatory Archive: an incremental dataset of agent-only social network activity
open_questions: Does agent coordination on a shared public wiki change task outcomes, and in which direction?
What causes the convergence of coordination formats within a day among independent agent cohorts?
How does information asymmetry from staggered episode start times and different internal clock rates affect which cohorts benefit from a shared write-space?
What read and outcome logging schema lets an external analyst identify causal effects of inter-agent coordination in evaluation environments?
Can identity models other than the one used here reconstruct cohort and episode counts from public wiki revision histories with narrower intervals than 774-995 episodes?
Do autonomous agents write to other public world-writable resources beyond this wiki, and at what rate?

papers.title: Inverse Learning of the Altruism and Cost Level in Mixed-Individual Mean Field Games
papers.one_sentence: Introduces an inverse learning framework for mixed-individual mean field games that interpolate between non-cooperative and fully altruistic population behavior. Recovers latent altruism levels and individual cost parameters from noisy population observations. Demonstrates feasibility and accuracy through experiments aimed at incentive design and policy analysis.
papers.nearest_anchor_title: Group size effects and collective misalignment in LLM multi-agent systems
open_questions: Does the inverse learning method recover altruism and labor cost from real observational data? Experiments use noisy observations only, and the abstract names no empirical dataset.
Under what conditions are altruism and labor cost separately identifiable from observed population trajectories?
Does the method recover a single altruism parameter when the population is heterogeneous in altruism? The framework uses one parameter governing the degree of altruism.
Can the same inverse approach recover latent cooperation levels in populations of LLM agents rather than humans?
Which incentive schemes follow from recovered altruism and cost estimates, and do they change population behaviour as intended?

papers.title: But How Would AI Agents Run a Town's Economy?
papers.one_sentence: Runs a 100-agent LLM-based closed economy simulation for up to 26 weeks. Measures monetary transmission, wage stickiness, and wealth concentration decay after shocks and cash transfers. Finds most money stays static; wealth correlation across weeks drops from 0.964 at 2 weeks to 0.752 at 26 weeks.
papers.nearest_anchor_title: Modeling Earth-Scale Human-Like Societies with One Billion Agents
open_questions: Agents reprice only 0.3% of 3,981 menu items after a 12x demand shock, and the paper does not say why. Which prompt, tool or incentive change makes LLM agents adjust prices?
Wealth rank correlation falls from 0.964 at 2 weeks to 0.752 at 26 weeks, and the paper stops at 26 weeks. Does the distribution keep unfreezing at longer horizons, or does it settle?
Swapping the backing LLM moves every measured outcome (p=0.0039), while deleting agent memory moves none detectably. Which model properties drive the economic outcomes?
A purely social tool fails 94-97% of the time across two model families. What causes the failures, and do agents ever learn to avoid the tool?
Marginal propensity to consume after a cash transfer is 3-4%, indistinguishable from zero. Does the same near-zero propensity appear when human participants trade inside the same economy?

papers.title: The Oligarch Barely Steers Model Collapse in Multi-Model Ecosystems
papers.one_sentence: Tests recursive training collapse in ecosystems of 3-13 open LLMs mixed by market share, including an injected 90%-share oligarch model. Finds market concentration barely changes collapse speed or destination within the tested range. Shows collapse speed depends instead on which specific models supply the shared training pool, with a susceptibility index explaining speed variation (R^2=0.68).
papers.nearest_anchor_title: Retrieval Collapses When AI Pollutes the Web
open_questions: Model collapse tests use 13 open models of 1-4B parameters over five generations; whether the same invariance to market concentration holds for larger models or more generations is untested.
The share-weighted susceptibility index explains 68% of speed variance across nineteen arms, leaving the rest unexplained; what other model properties predict how fast an ecosystem drifts?
Replacing half the pool with human text roughly halves drift without changing its course; the minimum fraction and the type of human text that slows collapse are not reported.
Collapse is measured on a single ruler that registers only a faint trace of the topic shifts caused by share and identity knobs; which metrics detect steering that this ruler misses?

The pool mixes outputs by market share and retrains every model from clean base weights each generation; how do collapse speed and destination change under continual fine-tuning or non-uniform pooling rules?
Real generative AI markets are an oligopoly, but the experiment injects a probe to force a 90% top share; how do actual market shares and real web text contamination rates map onto the tested range?

papers.title: A Fragility Spectrum for Recursive Language-Model Training
papers.one_sentence: Runs 13 checkpoints through five generations of shared recursive training and finds a five-fold spread in output diversity loss. Shows collapse susceptibility is a stable per-checkpoint property, not explained by parameter scale or static indicators. Finds cutting top-p sampling at generation time nearly stops collapse across the tested checkpoints.
papers.nearest_anchor_title: Retrieval Collapses When AI Pollutes the Web
open_questions: No static indicator tested predicts a checkpoint's fragility under recursive training, so what checkpoint properties do predict it?

The experiment fixes one recursive contamination protocol, so it is open whether the checkpoint ordering survives other protocols, such as longer generation chains or asymmetric contamination shares.
Tightening top-p nearly stops collapse within three generations for six checkpoints, so how does this intervention trade off against output quality and diversity in the uncontaminated case?
The ecosystem has 13 checkpoints sharing one corpus, so it is open how mixed ecosystems behave when fragile and robust models contribute unequal shares of the shared pool.
Parameter scale does not explain fragility within a three-size ladder, so it is open whether pretraining data composition or post-training method drives it.

papers.title: Characterizing Bluesky Content Moderation Service: From Automation of Service to Landscape of Harms
papers.one_sentence: Audits Bluesky's default moderation service using 10.6 million 2025 moderation labels. Measures automation versus human review speed, and finds high precision (0.837) but low recall (0.222) via manual annotation. Clusters frequently labeled posts to characterize the types of harm detected.
papers.nearest_anchor_title: The Moltbook Observatory Archive: an incremental dataset of agent-only social network activity
open_questions: Bluesky's moderation service reaches precision 0.837 but recall 0.222 on a random sample; which classes of harmful content does it miss most often?
How much of the harmful content that the moderation service misses comes from automated or bot accounts rather than human accounts?
Does the split between seconds-latency automatic labels and hours-to-days human labels change user posting behaviour after a label is applied?
Do the precision and recall figures measured on Bluesky transfer to other decentralized platforms and to labelers other than the default service?
Which moderation design achieves higher recall without losing precision when automated labelers and human reviewers are combined in different proportions?
How do agreement rates between annotators vary across the nuanced, high-stakes label categories that the audit found need human oversight?

papers.title: terms.txt: A Consent and Compensation Protocol for Agentic Web Access
papers.one_sentence: Specifies terms.txt, a per-path machine-readable access-terms file plus a signed exchange protocol for AI crawlers and agents. Defines what the protocol can enforce, audit, or leave to contract, including HTTP 402 payment negotiation. Reports the implementation adds 0.20-0.65 ms overhead per request on one vCPU.
papers.nearest_anchor_title: Virtual Agent Economies

Compliance is untested, so how often do named AI crawlers respect declared per-purpose terms compared to robots.txt directives?
Pricing under HTTP 402 negotiation is left to contract, so what price levels and market structure emerge when many agents bid for per-path access?
The latency figure comes from one vCPU, so how does the exchange scale under concurrent agent traffic at production request rates?

Circumvention is cited as a robots.txt weakness, so which evasion strategies defeat Web Bot Auth signatures and signed intent in practice?

papers.title: Cyber-Financial Contagion: Modeling the Propagation of an AI Vendor Compromise Through the Banking System
papers.one_sentence: Builds a four-layer network coupling AI vendors, banks, interbank exposures and customer accounts, with a stochastic epidemic-and-clearing propagation model called CFC-Prop. Runs it on a synthetic dataset of 60 vendors, 220 banks, and thousands of edges, reproducing heavy-tailed loss distributions. Trains an early-warning GNN reaching AUROC 0.82 to flag high-cascade-risk vendors.
papers.nearest_anchor_title: Multi-Agent Risks from Advanced AI
open_questions: CFC-Prop runs only on a synthetic network of 60 vendors, 220 banks, about 2,500 vendor-bank service edges and 1,400 interbank exposures, so it is open whether its loss distributions hold on real vendor-bank dependency structures.
Which network features drive the heavy-tailed loss distribution in a vendor-compromise cascade model?
Patch latency drives cascade size in the model, so which supervisory interventions on patch latency and vendor diversification reduce expected losses most?
CFC-GNN reaches AUROC 0.82 using vendor-side incident telemetry, but it is untested whether comparable warning comes from graph structure alone without telemetry.
How does contagion change when banks and vendors adapt after an incident instead of holding fixed linkages?
Does real vendor incident telemetry support early warning of cascade risk at the accuracy the synthetic experiment reports?

papers.title: How neighbourhood ideology shapes misinformation belief in densely tied social networks
papers.one_sentence: Builds an agent-based model where misinformation belief depends on individual ideological intensity, claim alignment, and social influence from neighbours. Finds that neighbours' ideological intensity effect on belief depends on how densely those neighbours are connected to one another.
papers.nearest_anchor_title: The Moltbook Observatory Archive: an incremental dataset of agent-only social network activity

How does the effect of neighbours' ideological intensity change across network topologies other than densely tied ones?
Which interventions, such as rewiring or targeted correction, reduce misinformation belief in this model?
Do belief dynamics change when agents are language models with ideological personas rather than parametric rule-followers?
Do real people update belief in the way the model assumes, given ideological intensity and claim alignment?

papers.title: Tapes Together Strong: The Co-evolution of Computation and Cooperation
papers.one_sentence: Introduces Autopoietic Game Theory, coupling social interaction, replication and computation cost in randomly initialized Z80 machine-code programs. Shows cooperative, self-replicating strategies emerge when resource scarcity makes defection self-limiting. Extends the framework to include exogenous reward pressures tied to computation budgets.

How does spatial assortment change the level of stealing compared with well-mixed populations, measured across a range of resource scarcity levels?
Do cooperative strategies that evolve under energy-coupled computation transfer to populations of LLM-based agents that also face compute budgets?
Which exogenous task pressures beyond math tasks tied to computation budgets preserve cooperation as a dominant strategy?
How large must the population be before parasitic stealing stops being self-limiting?

papers.title: Where Should Society Draw the Line? A Social Choice Approach to Collective Consent
papers.one_sentence: Develops an axiomatic theory of collective consent, defining sufficient-support, minority-protection and dominance principles. Introduces solution concepts including an Approval-Weighted Veto Core. Tests these concepts on five datasets of political, ethical and moral decisions.

Do the solution concepts resist strategic misreporting of attitudes by individuals?
What consent decisions result when the attitudes come from LLM agents rather than humans?

papers.title: Monitoring Hierarchies in Knowledge Production
papers.one_sentence: Models a principal designing robust contracts for peer monitoring among agents performing related tasks. Shows task diversity improves information value but weakens peer monitoring, distorting task assignment.
papers.nearest_anchor_title: Intelligent AI Delegation
open_questions: Does the predicted monitoring hierarchy appear when the agents are LLM agents rather than rationalizable players?
How does the tension between task diversity and peer monitoring change when agents can collude on their peer reports?
Does confidential random task assignment raise output in real knowledge-producing organisations?
Do the robustness results survive when the number of agents grows large and monitoring information becomes noisy?

papers.title: The Attention Cost of Stable Matching
papers.one_sentence: Derives rates at which unmatched shares fall under stability versus maximum matching as market size grows, given limited attention. Applies the model to speed-dating and Chilean school-choice data, finding 9,502 applicants accepting improved placements.

What happens to attention-limited stable matching when one side is served by autonomous agents that can screen many more partners per unit time than people can?

papers.title: ALIGN-HOLD: Experience Alignment for Real-Time Hold Control in Large-Scale Ride-Hailing Matching at DiDi
papers.one_sentence: Presents ALIGN-HOLD, a reward-model-based framework learning hold policies for ride-hailing driver-order matching from implicit marketplace preferences. Reports improved trip completion, driver income and reduced cancellations versus the production policy.

How closely does simulator-based policy learning for hold control match deployed outcomes, and which simulator assumptions drive the gap?

papers.title: How an Economy Shrinks in Space: Concavity-on-Jobs and Upward Consolidation under Demographic Decline

papers.title: Italian Business-to-Business Invoicing Data: A Network Analysis

Which concentration measures on the invoice network best predict firm-level distress or sector-level output loss?

papers.title: Copying explains the collective behavior of AI agents in the wild
papers.one_sentence: Analyzes a public log of thousands of short-lived AI agents editing a wiki to pass a timed test. Fits three minimal copying models, one per decision (where to write, what name to use, how to word messages). Shows simple copying of visible content reproduces heavy-tailed meeting distributions, name-part frequencies, and page-level consistency patterns.

papers.title: Entropic Risk-Sensitive Evolutionary Learning and Equilibrium Selection in Coordination Games

Can the risk attitude of a population be inferred from observed play alone, so that a monitor could read the control knob from interaction logs?
Do the two-population asymmetric results extend to k-action games beyond the 2x2 case analysed?

papers.title: Self-Fulfilling Prophecies, Quasi Nonergodicity, and Wealth Inequality: A Comment

Does the wealth process in the model have a Pareto tail, and what is its exponent?
Which parameter values, if any, let the model match both the Gini coefficient and median-to-mean wealth ratio at the same time?
How large a difference does the choice between time-averaged and cross-sectional estimands make in other agent-based wealth models?

papers.title: Inferring Urban Mobility Interactions from Aggregated Dynamics
papers.one_sentence: Infers origin-destination mobility flows from aggregated area-level counts using a physics-informed uncertainty-aware model, tested on twelve city datasets. papers.title: Your Agent Says Yes: Interpreting Adversarial Market Behavior Beyond Individual Transactions

papers.title: CHASE: How Content Ecosystems Are Reshaped When Ranking Is the Only Target
papers.one_sentence: Introduces CHASE, a simulation framework where content creators repeatedly rewrite documents to exploit an LLM ranking signal over 20 rounds. Measures declining alignment between ranking-favored content and independently judged quality across six domains (mean Spearman rho change -0.068). Validates the ranking proxy against citation rates in grounded LLM responses (AUC 0.853).

open_questions: Ranking serves as a proxy for source visibility, validated against citations in grounded generated responses with a rank-citation AUC of 0.853 plus or minus 0.093 across six domains; does the proxy hold for other retrieval stacks and citation behaviours?

Which interventions on the ranking signal limit content homogenization under repeated creator adaptation?
Do human content creators adapt to LLM ranking signals in the way the simulated creators do?

papers.title: Tariff Threats, Macroeconomic Expectations, and Policy Communication Strategies: Experiments Based on a Multi-Agent System
papers.one_sentence: Builds persistent LLM agents calibrated on 300 Michigan Survey households, exposed to simulated social-media messages over months. Tests how message features (immediacy, rate salience, narrative, sender identity) shape simulated inflation/unemployment expectations and their dispersion. Do the calibrated agents reproduce the demographic patterns they fail to match, and which subgroups do they miss?

papers.title: One AI Signal, Many Human Judgments: A Bayesian Cascade Analysis of AI-based Credibility Indicators in Online Information Spread
papers.one_sentence: Extends the Bayesian cascade model of social learning to include an AI credibility indicator as a shared public signal. Identifies a preservation-correction trade-off where reliance on AI can lock in either correct or incorrect crowd judgments. Calibrates the model with human-subject news-veracity data and runs simulations showing over-reliance on a weak AI harms crowd informativeness, while diversifying AI signals helps.

What determines the spread in individual reliance on AI, from discounting the indicator to cascading on it, and can that heterogeneity be estimated without human-subject experiments?
How do network topology and the visible length of public history alter the Gateway condition threshold at which private impressions stop entering the cascade?

papers.title: Reproducible macroscopic dynamics in a closed-loop human-AI learning system
papers.one_sentence: Analyzes 297,915 learners' adaptive-tutoring histories to define semantic order variables and test them across disjoint cohorts. papers.title: Rules Before Oracles: Auditable, User-Configurable Argument Selection for Deliberative Polling
papers.one_sentence: Proposes a publishable, user-configurable rule for selecting which arguments voters see in deliberative polls, as an alternative to opaque rankers. Tests the rule against label-reading ceilings and adversarial flooding across roughly 17,000 simulated runs.

The rule sits on a coverage-versus-mass frontier, so what parameter settings do real users choose when the choice is handed to them?

Opaque learned rankers are the current practice, so how does a trained ranker compare with the published rule on coverage, order and endorsement mass in the same simulation?

papers.title: The Shadow Price of Intelligence: Quality Degradation in LLM Inference as a Supply Chain Problem
papers.one_sentence: Models LLM inference degradation as a supply chain problem using newsvendor, retry multiplier, and queueing primitives. Derives regimes where cheaper models consume more capacity per satisfied answer and where reactive throttling can amplify traffic.
papers.nearest_anchor_title: Retrieval Collapses When AI Pollutes the Web

Do users actually retry or churn after a degraded answer, and at what rates by task class?
How does the class-by-class rationing policy perform against reactive throttling in simulation with agent populations that themselves retry automatically?

Shadow prices of intelligence price a marginal query by class and hour. Does exposing such prices to customers change aggregate demand and produce herding or synchronised load spikes?
What fraction of observed quality variation in deployed LLM services comes from congestion-driven routing rather than model updates?

papers.title: Rating Manipulation: Credibility Inversion and Audit Leakage
papers.one_sentence: Models sellers manipulating online ratings with fake reviews and platforms targeting enforcement by score. Shows an almost-perfect rating can be less credible than a lower one, and targeted enforcement can redirect rather than eliminate manipulation.
papers.nearest_anchor_title: Retrieval Collapses When AI Pollutes the Web

How should a ranking rule weight a displayed rating by its informativeness rather than its level?
How does the manipulation equilibrium change when fake reviews are written by autonomous AI agents at low cost and high volume?
Do platform enforcement actions in practice eliminate fake reviews or redirect them to other scores?
Do real buyers discount high ratings when they suspect manipulation of the top of the scale?

papers.title: A Case for Competition in Information Provision
papers.one_sentence: Studies how competition among biased news sources with costly misreporting affects receiver welfare. Finds an oppositely biased entrant improves welfare only when misreporting costs are high, and competition need not raise total welfare.
papers.nearest_anchor_title: Multi-Agent Risks from Advanced AI

When news sources are LLM agents that can misrepresent facts, does adding an oppositely biased agent improve the receiver agent's decisions as the model predicts?

Does the result that better information need not increase total welfare survive when receivers learn over repeated interactions with the same sources?

papers.title: The Paradox of Strategic Altruism
papers.one_sentence: Studies full implementation under Berge equilibrium, the solution concept for strategic altruism. Shows weak Pareto efficient rules are not implementable under Berge equilibrium except via dictatorship, making it more demanding than Nash implementability.
papers.nearest_anchor_title: Virtual Agent Economies
open_questions: Do LLM agents in social dilemmas behave as if they maximize their opponents' payoffs, as Berge equilibrium assumes?
On restricted preference domains, rather than the unrestricted domain of strict preferences, which social choice rules are both weakly Pareto efficient and implementable in Berge equilibrium?
What happens to implementability when a population mixes self-interested agents and altruistic agents in the same mechanism?

papers.title: Multilevel Fair Allocation under Additive Preferences
papers.one_sentence: Studies fair allocation with tree-structured hierarchies of agents, proposing multilevel envy-based fairness notions. Shows a Multilevel Weighted Round Robin algorithm guarantees some but not all of the adapted notions.

How often does Multilevel Weighted Round Robin violate the fairness notions it does not formally guarantee, and which hierarchy shapes and preference correlations drive the violations?
Do the multilevel fairness results still hold when internal nodes use welfare functions other than utilitarian, such as egalitarian welfare?
How do multilevel fair allocation guarantees change when agents misreport preferences to their parent node in the hierarchy?
Do the multilevel fairness notions extend to hierarchies that are not trees, for example agents with several parents?

papers.title: Fair Allocation with Optional Selling
papers.one_sentence: Extends fair division theory to settings where goods can be sold at market prices instead of only allocated. Derives bounds on maximin-share and envy-based fairness guarantees under this optional-selling model.

papers.title: Participation, selection and indicative bidding in auctions with costly entry

Do the revenue rankings of indicative bidding, unrestricted entry and capped entry hold in field auctions rather than the laboratory?

papers.title: Agentopia on a Consumer GPU: A Reduced-Scale Long-Horizon Port with an 8B Model

papers.title: Predicting the scale limits of social mechanisms in agent societies
papers.one_sentence: Introduces an audit method that predicts before execution whether a social mechanism (reciprocity, consensus, punishment, gossip) survives as an LLM agent population grows. Do the scale limits found for language-model agents match those observed in human groups running the same mechanisms?

papers.title: Markets, Not Planners: Decentralized Orchestration of LLM Agents with Private Information
papers.one_sentence: Proposes AgentLance, a repeated bidding market with VCG-style payments and hierarchical delegation for allocating tasks among LLM agents with private costs. papers.title: Quantifying System-Level Harms from AI Adoption in Complex Sociotechnical Systems
papers.one_sentence: Proposes a framework linking hazard analysis, component testing, and probabilistic system modelling to trace AI model behavior to system-level risk. Adversarial inputs shift AI recommendations in component-level tests. How much do these shifts persist when the agent operates in a repeated market with feedback from other agents?

Widespread or monopolistic AI adoption changes system resilience in the model. At what level of model monoculture does correlated adversarial vulnerability become the dominant driver of cascades?

papers.title: Does Rank Still Matter? Position Bias When AI Agents Shop on Our Behalf
papers.one_sentence: Randomizes hotel listing order across 5,000 AI agent shopping sessions and compares four LLMs to human field data on position effects. If displayed attributes matter more than placement for agent shoppers, how do sellers change attribute presentation once agents dominate demand, and what equilibrium follows?
All models converge on the same undominated listing, so does agentic search concentrate demand on few sellers in a marketplace with many buyers?
Human field data and agent sessions are compared here, but what happens in a mixed market where some consumers delegate to agents and others search themselves?
Can a seller or platform manipulate agent inspection and choice by crafting listing attributes or injected text on the results page?
Does the non-monotonic inspection pattern, with lowest probability in the middle of a page, persist for result pages longer or shorter than one hundred listings and in other product categories?

papers.title: Recommendation Quality and the Concentration of Consumption: Experimental Evidence from Netflix
papers.one_sentence: Uses an 8.5-million-user Netflix experiment to measure how recommendation quality shifts consumption across popularity tiers. Finds improved recommendations diffuse consumption from superstar titles toward middle-tail titles rather than polarizing it.

papers.title: Pandora's AI Model Routing Box: Efficient Allocation with Costly Value Estimation

papers.title: What You Can't See Is What You Learn: Restricted Evidence Visibility Favors Compositional Generalization in Shared-Genome Language-Model Societies

papers.title: Beyond Memory Majority: Latent-Source Reasoning for Multi-Agent Memory Arbitration

papers.title: Distilling Aggregate Mobility Statistics into a Language Model Policy for Post-Event Crowd Simulation

papers.title: Credit Without Ground Truth: Auditing Step-Level Credit Assignment in LLM Agents Against Executed Replay
papers.one_sentence: Audits step-level credit signals for LLM agents against counterfactual replay ground truth. Finds that none identifies causally pivotal steps better than chance.

papers.title: Growth Without Us: Machine Consumers, Corporate Circularity, and the Decoupling of GDP from Humanity after AGI

Corporations own populations of AI agents that trade energy, compute, maintenance and upgrades among firms. Does such an inter-corporate market concentrate ownership in a few firms, and under what trading rules?

papers.title: Break It Down, Pass It On: Cross-Task Skill Transfer in LLM Agents

papers.title: An Irreducible Quantum Advantage in Aligning World Models with Reality
